p:cNvPr.descr: A cross-section of the cell membrane and how the GLUT1 transporter is organized in relation to the membrane. The membrane has pale blue hydrophilic heads and yellow hydrophobic tails arranged toward the inside. The top of the membrane is labeled “outside” and the bottom is labeled “inside.” The GLUT1 transporter is a long chain of residues in blue, yellow, and red which winds in a helical fashion into and out of the membrane. A key at the top right shows the colors and meanings of the dots that make up the transporter. In this box, yellow means hydrophobic residue, blue means polar residue, and red means charged residue. The chain of residues winds up and down, in and out of the membrane, with most of its hydrophobic residues concentrated inside the membrane. The residue loops above and below the membrane as well. There are more charged residues outside the membrane than inside, and slightly more polar residues outside the membrane than inside. On the left side of the membrane, the end of the chain hangs down and is bonded down to +NH3. On the far right end, a long winding chain is bonded to COO-.

p:cNvPr.descr: The helical wheel diagram of GLUT1 is a ball-and-stick helix viewed from above. The sequence of residues is written above: Ser—Leu—Val—Thr—Asn—Phe—Ile. The residues are labeled and numbered and descend as their numbers increase. If they bond down, they move away from the viewer. The left most ball is a blue Ser (1), which bonds up & right to a yellow Leu (2), which bonds down to a yellow Val (3), which bonds down and left to a blue Thr (4), which bonds down to a blue Asn (5), which bonds right to a yellow Phe (6), which bonds down to a yellow Ile (7), and so on. The remaining residues are not numbered.

p:cNvPr.descr: A simple cartoon showing the association of the helices with one another. A central Glc, represented by a blue hexagon, is surrounded by a circle of blue circles, and 4 “flower petal” arrangements of yellow circles around those.

p:cNvPr.descr: Cross-section of the GLUT1 transporter as it traverses the membrane. It is a red, blue, and yellow surface contour model, but the contours and colors face away from the viewer. The inside of the protein is somewhat gray and featureless; the central cavity is toward the bottom and the residues fold inside the protein here. The cavity is long and vertical and is labeled to the left.
